title: Rotting Oranges
summary: Rot spreads from every rotten orange to its neighbours each minute; find when the last fresh orange rots.

tests.explain: The rot spreads one step per minute: (0,1) at minute 1, (0,2) and (1,1) at 2, (2,1) at 3, (2,0) and (2,2) at 4, (2,3) at 5 and finally (1,3) at 6.
The oranges at (2,0) and (2,2) have no rotten neighbour, ever: empty cells cut them off. So it's impossible: -1.
There are no fresh oranges at all, so no time needs to pass: 0.

hints: All rotten oranges start spreading at the same time. Running a separate search from each one gives the wrong timing.
Put every rotten orange in one queue before you start (multi-source BFS). Process the queue one level at a time: one level is one minute.
Count the fresh oranges up front and decrease the count as they rot. If any are left when the queue runs dry, return -1. With no fresh oranges the answer is 0.

complexity.time: O(m·n): each cell is queued at most once
complexity.space: O(m·n): the queue can hold every orange
